items.title: 52263_Sonny Greer oral history interview
items.q: We were in California making a picture and Tommy Dorsey, he said to me, I'll never forget said 'That's the greatest trombone player in the world.'

ctx.x: exaggeration, Lawrence Brown was the greatest trombone player I ever heard in my life. Lawrence Brown, you remember Lawrence Brown trying to make -- well, they were always looking for a ofay--- king --/today in prizefighting, but anyway Lawrence Brown, I know one time on a recording session, if Barney Bigard, on clarinet, if he didn't show or was late for the recording, he would give Lawrence Brown a clarinet part. Ever heard of that, a trombone player playing a clarinet part?

And he would run it clean as a whistle. We were in California making a picture and Tommy Dorsey, he said to me, I'll never forget said 'That's the greatest trombone player in the world.' And Lawrence Brown didn't know what he could do, you better believe it. Barney, and a bass player -- Charlie Mingus just died.
